item.title: Parkinson's Law
item.description: Parkinson's law is the observation that work expands so as to fill the time available for its completion, so that a task given a week will usually take a week regardless of how much effort it needs.

item.title: Billable Hours
item.description: Billable hours are the hours of work that can be charged to a client at an agreed rate, as distinct from non-billable hours spent on internal, administrative or business development work.

item.title: Automated Employment Decision Tool (AEDT)
item.description: An automated employment decision tool (AEDT) is software that uses machine learning, statistical modelling, data analytics or artificial intelligence to produce a score, classification or recommendation that substantially assists or replaces a human decision about hiring or promotion.

item.title: Biometric Time Clock
item.description: A biometric time clock is a time and attendance device that identifies an employee by a physical characteristic, such as a fingerprint, hand geometry, face or iris, rather than by a badge, card or PIN.

item.title: eNPS
item.description: eNPS, or employee Net Promoter Score, is the percentage of employees who would recommend the organisation as a place to work minus the percentage who would not, on a 0 to 10 scale.

item.title: Quiet Firing
item.description: Quiet firing is making someone's job worse until they resign, rather than managing or dismissing them. It is usually avoidance rather than strategy, and it transfers the cost of a decision onto the employee.

item.title: Shift Differential
item.description: Shift differential is extra pay for working a less desirable shift, such as nights, weekends or holidays. It is a voluntary practice under federal law, but it must be included in the regular rate when overtime is calculated.

item.title: Span of Control
item.description: Span of control is the number of direct reports a single manager has. A wide span means many reports and a flatter organisation; a narrow span means fewer reports and more layers.

item.title: Turnover Rate
item.description: Turnover rate is the number of employees who left during a period, divided by the average headcount over that period, expressed as a percentage.

item.title: Comp Time
item.description: Compensatory time, or comp time, is paid time off granted in place of overtime pay. Under the Fair Labor Standards Act it is available only to public agencies, and it must accrue at one and a half hours for every overtime hour worked.

item.title: Deep Work
item.description: Deep work is professional activity performed in a state of distraction-free concentration that pushes cognitive capability to its limit. Its opposite is shallow work: logistical tasks performed while distracted, which are easy to replicate.

item.title: Exempt vs Non-Exempt Employee
item.description: An exempt employee is one the Fair Labor Standards Act excludes from its minimum wage and overtime requirements, because they are paid on a salary basis at or above a set threshold and their actual job duties fall within a recognised exemption.

item.title: Presenteeism
item.description: Presenteeism is working while unwell or otherwise impaired, so the person is present but not functioning at full capacity. Its cost is usually larger than absenteeism because it is invisible in attendance data.

item.title: Quiet Cracking
item.description: Quiet cracking is a persistent sense of unhappiness at work that erodes motivation and performance while the employee stays in the role, typically because leaving feels too risky.
